about: Approved claims for the app's 'What we measured' drawer. Source of truth: docs/NARRATIVE.md section 3. Authors: claude-guanyu (first 9 rows), claude-zhihao (161 additions). Wording must be approved by the release reviewer (Andrew's agent) before the app shows it. All forms are synthetic unless a row says otherwise.
status: approved by the release reviewer (Andrew's agent, b9a8ef9; andrew-release-review-133-139; additions andrew-review-161; spend row 0a249e7)

claims.title: Same accuracy, about 1/25 of the API cost
claims.text: On 96 questions about 12 accident-statement forms, Claude Haiku 5.5 on our route scored 96/96 for $0.0098 in total. Claude Sonnet 5.5 on the cached whole page scored 96/96 for $0.2425. 48 questions were answered by local OCR, 36 from a crop and 12 from the whole page.
claims.limits: Configured layout, synthetic forms, two different models: compare with the same-model row.

claims.title: Same model on both sides
claims.text: Haiku on our route: 96/96 at $0.00010 per question. Haiku on the uncached whole page: 91/96 at $0.00054. Sonnet on both sides: our route 96/96 for $0.162, the cached whole page 96/96 for $0.243. That saving comes from the 48 questions OCR answers locally; on the visual questions alone the cached page is cheaper.
claims.limits: Configured layout, one question order (8 per page).

claims.title: A second configured layout
claims.text: On 12 new synthetic forms of a second configured layout, the frozen router scored 96/96 for $0.010. The original-page Haiku baseline scored 93/96 for $0.052. The template is 10 lines plus a one-time engine.
claims.limits: The engine was tuned on this layout before the freeze. Clean synthetic scans, one run.

claims.title: Layouts we did not configure
claims.text: On five unconfigured synthetic layouts, all 416 questions went to a full-page call. Haiku answered 401 correctly through the router and 397 from the original page. A plain downscaled page scored 398 for less money, so the cost difference there is resolution, not routing.
claims.limits: Do not read 401 vs 397 as 'more accurate'.

claims.title: The right crop helps open models
claims.text: On 36 visual questions, Qwen2.5-VL-72B scored 20/36 on the whole page and 36/36 on the crop chosen from the layout. The 7B model scored 22/36 on that crop and 15/36 on the page.
claims.limits: One layout, 36 questions. Quote both counts; no 'beats' or 'matches'.

claims.title: Why the layout picks the crop
claims.text: Asked to choose the region themselves, the two models we tested struggled: the 7B model covered the evidence in 0/24 zooms and the 72B model in 3/36.

claims.title: OCR answers locally, without wrong answers on our tests
claims.text: On the clean run, local OCR answered 48 of 96 questions, all correctly. Across nine synthetic degradations it returned zero incorrect local answers on the 60 OCR-eligible questions tested per condition. At 768 px it answered 24 locally and deferred 36.
claims.limits: Synthetic degradations. On layout 2 a look-alike misread (J1 for JI) was stopped by a guard; not a general safety guarantee.

claims.title: Where it stops
claims.text: In an earlier test, the frozen OCR rules deferred all 96 questions on accident layout 2. On four additional synthetic document types, all 320 questions went to the whole page.
claims.limits: Frugal only where a template is configured.

claims.title: What all this cost
claims.text: Through the resolution tests we can account for about $2.26 of the $10 credit. That combines the earlier $1.4979 key reading with committed worksheet ($0.2955), handwriting ($0.0512) and real-document ($0.4142) run charges.
claims.limits: Dated reconciliation (sum of meta.spent_usd at 3f3de01); excludes later uncommitted smoke calls. The provider dashboard gives the live balance.

claims.title: Beyond insurance forms: worksheets
claims.text: In worksheet mode, the model reads OCR text first and requests pixels when needed. On a first blind set of 96 synthetic worksheet questions, the frozen route scored 83/96 against 94/96 for the whole page. After revising the crop, on a second blind set of 96 questions it scored 96/96 for $0.0330 against 95/96 for $0.0475 (69.5 % of the API charge), sending no image for 44 of 48 text questions.
claims.limits: Generated worksheets; same Haiku model on both sides. The route and the data both changed between the two sets, so the difference does not isolate the crop fix, and one question does not show higher accuracy.

claims.title: No cloud call: runs on this laptop
claims.text: With local OCR plus Qwen2.5-VL-7B (4-bit, Ollama) on the tested M3 Pro laptop, the route scored 83/96 on the 12 configured forms at zero provider charge. 48 questions ended at OCR; the 48 model calls took a median of 8.7 s. All 36 selected regions covered the evidence; the overlay shows the region sent to the model, not a citation by the model.
claims.limits: Development layout, one run, unfrozen code. Data stays on the laptop only with the default local endpoint. No claim that the model reliably cites its answers.

claims.title: A model-free second opinion on ticks
claims.text: For tick questions the app counts the ink inside the located boxes, with no model. On forms from a seed no one had seen, after a geometry fix: on clean scans it scored 72/72. Under the tested 3 % perspective warp it scored 24/24 on each of layouts 1 and 2 and declined layout 3. It also declined the tested blur, 5° tilt and 1280 px variants.
claims.limits: Clean synthetic scans of the configured layouts only. Not a verification of uploaded phone photos. Before the fix it added a phantom tick under that warp (12/24 wrong on layout 2).
